data.narrative:
Vinci is an AI & Software company founded by Hardik Kabaria, Sarah Osentoski, and Vincent Rerolle. The analysis drew from a comp universe of 12 same-sector peers, comprising 1 public company (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private firms including Palantir, Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. The target's stage, current valuation, and total capital raised remain undisclosed.

A peer-median valuation approach was deemed inapplicable due to insufficient narrow peer data. Despite identifying 12 companies within AI & Software, filtering by stage, adjacency, and valuation tier yielded fewer than the required three comparable datapoints. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material noise given the heterogeneity of AI & Software business models, margins, and growth trajectories. No triangulated valuation range could therefore be supported through quantitative multiples analysis.

Meaningful valuation of Vinci requires either (1) disclosure of stage, revenue, or growth metrics to enable narrower peer selection; (2) expansion of the comp set to adjacent software or infrastructure sectors; or (3) application of bottom-up methods (DCF, market sizing) grounded in company-specific financial or operational data. Without these inputs, quantitative analysis remains incomplete. The single public comparable (PLTR) alone is insufficient to establish a defensible range.
